content.alt: The Wizard of Oz - What kind of story is The Wizard of Oz?
content.text:
What kind of story is The Wizard of Oz?

The Wizard of Oz is an adventure classic about a girl named Dorothy who is swept away by a whirlwind to the magical land of Oz and, together with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion, searches for the way home. Its warm message is that what you truly need is already inside you.

content.alt: The Wizard of Oz - The original story of The Wizard of Oz
content.text:
The original story of The Wizard of Oz

The original is The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, published by the American author L. Frank Baum in 1900. It is filled with iconic elements such as the yellow brick road, the Emerald City, and the Wizard of Oz, and it was also greatly loved as a 1939 film.

content.alt: The Wizard of Oz - The Wizard of Oz story summary
content.text:
The Wizard of Oz story summary

Swept to Oz by a whirlwind, Dorothy sets out to find the Wizard of Oz so she can return home. Along the road she meets the Scarecrow who wants wisdom, the Tin Woodman who wants a warm heart, and the Lion who wants courage, and they journey together. At the end of the adventure, they realize that what they wished for was already inside them all along.

content.alt: The Wizard of Oz - The lesson of The Wizard of Oz
content.text:
The lesson of The Wizard of Oz

The core message is that precious things like wisdom, love, and courage are already inside you, and friends who journey alongside you are a great source of strength. Talk with your child about "What wonderful qualities do I already have?"

content.alt: The Wizard of Oz - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Acting out the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Lion with different voices deepens the immersion. Ask "Was the Scarecrow really without any wisdom?" so your child can discover for themselves that each friend already had what they were looking for. Best suited for ages 4 to 7.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Wizard of Oz good for?
A. Best suited for ages 4 to 7. Its blend of adventure and a warm message makes it widely loved.

Q. Who are Dorothy's friends?
A. The Scarecrow who wants wisdom, the Tin Woodman who wants a heart, and the Lion who wants courage.

Q. What conversations pair well with it?
A. Talk together about "the wonderful qualities I already have" and "the good things about being with friends."

Classic tales to read together

If you enjoyed this story, try reading these classic tales together too.

  • The Frog Prince
  • The Ant and the Grasshopper
  • The Selfish Giant
  • Gulliver's Travels
